data.one_liner: Lightweight Flutter MVVM implementation with state sharing via global registry or inherited widgets.
data.what_it_does: Organizes UI into View widgets and business logic into ViewModels extending ChangeNotifier. It includes a built-in locator for sharing states either globally or through inherited widgets, along with convenience property types like ValueNotifier, FutureProperty, and StreamProperty.
use_when: You want to structure your Flutter application using the MVVM pattern.
You need lightweight state management combined with a simple dependency locator similar to GetIt or Provider.
avoid_when: You prefer strict event-driven state architectures like BLoC/Cubit.
Your project standardizes entirely around Riverpod for state management.
strengths: Simple and small API extending native Flutter classes.
Supports both global registry and widget tree (inherited) locations for ViewModels.
Includes specialized properties like FutureProperty and StreamProperty for easy async data handling.
weaknesses: Requires learning its specific MVVM widget and view model extension patterns.
Less ecosystem tooling compared to major state management libraries like Provider or Riverpod.

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer standard InheritedWidget-based dependency injection and state management without the strict MVVM class hierarchy.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want compile-safe global state management without relying on BuildContext or registries.

alternatives.name: flutter_bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a strict predictable state machine architecture separating events and states.
